description:
We’re a team from Oman interested in space, technology, and sharing the stories of NASA’s past missions.
We’re looking for creative teammates with skills in coding, design, or storytelling to build something fun and educational.
summary:
Developed by Team SUHD for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, Last Signal is an interactive, bilingual (Arabic and English) web-based learning experience centered on NASA’s Opportunity rover.
o address the challenge of abandoned space missions fading from public awareness, the platform enables students aged 12 to 16 to reconstruct the mission's history using authentic NASA data—including 3D models and Photo journal images—rather than simply reading pre-made conclusions. Learners interactively test hypotheses about Martian spheres and evaluate real solar power data to derive scientific insights firsthand.
This project is vital because it shifts students from passive readers to active scientific investigators, expands access to authentic space science data in Arabic, runs seamlessly on mobile and desktop devices without installation, and directly supports UN Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education).
details:
Space agencies have left a lasting record of hardware on the Moon and Mars, yet the stories behind these missions rarely reach school students in a form they can understand or question. This proposal presents Last Signal, a bilingual (Arabic and English) web-based learning experience developed by Team SUHD for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge “Abandoned but not Forgotten”.

The experience focuses on NASA’s Opportunity rover, which was designed for a 90-day mission, remained active for more than 14 years and sent its final transmission on 10 June 2018. Rather than presenting conclusions, Last Signal asks students aged 12 to 16 to rebuild the rover’s story from NASA’s own evidence: the official 3D model, original images from the NASA Photo journal and published measurements. Learners examine how dust and wind affected the rover’s solar power, test four competing explanations for the small spheres found at Meridiani Planum and reach the same conclusion as the mission scientists: the spheres are evidence of ancient water, not of life.

A mission guide answers questions using verified NASA facts only, and each learner finishes with a personalized legacy card that carries a QR code inviting other students to take part. The proposal reviews existing resources, compares three design options against defined selection criteria, identifies requirements, constraints and risks, and sets out a work plan and expected outcomes aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education).
